article_title: Equipping Science Teachers to Support Student Motivation in NGSS Classrooms: Insights from the Development of the M-PLANS Program
citation: Harris, C.J., Schmidt, J.A., Linnenbrink-Garcia, L., Marchand, G.C., Cabrera, L., McKinney, D., & Liu, P. (2023). Equipping science teachers to support student motivation in NGSS classrooms: Insights from the Development of the M-PLANS program. San Francisco, CA: WestEd. https://m-plans.org/
title: M-PLANS five motivation design principles for science instruction
description: M-PLANS uses five theoretically and empirically based motivation design principles (MDPs): Belonging, Confidence, Learning Orientation, Autonomy, and Relevance. These MDPs translate general motivation principles into science-specific instructional practice so teachers can readily embed them in instruction, with sample metacognitive planning questions for each principle. The principles are heuristics, not prescriptions, meant to be used flexibly to meet diverse students' needs.
requirements: Teachers use the MDPs as heuristics in planning and instruction, considering their students and remaining attuned to them throughout the school year.
constraints: The principles are principles, not prescriptions, so each teacher integrates them in their own ways to meet the needs of their unique sets of students.
target_learning_goals: Student motivation and engagement in NGSS-based science learning
examples: Figure 1 presents each MDP with accompanying reflective questions teachers can use to incorporate each MDP into their lesson planning and instruction.

title: M-PLANS professional learning program and resource suite
description: The Motivation - Planning Lessons to Activate eNgagement in Science (M-PLANS) program aims to equip science teachers to support students' motivation and engagement in NGSS-based instruction. It includes a multi-week professional learning approach, a comprehensive reference toolkit, and pocket-sized classroom-based quick tools for lesson planning and just-in-time instructional decisions. Resources were iteratively developed and tested in middle school science classrooms.
requirements: Teachers attend an initial professional learning institute, followed by ongoing support during the school year via a professional learning community that promotes collective inquiry and reflective dialogue.
target_learning_goals: Robust and meaningful science learning through motivationally supportive instruction
examples: More than 20 science teachers across 12 racially and ethnically diverse middle schools contributed to the development process.

title: M-PLANS reference toolkit and classroom-based quick tools
description: The toolkit is a comprehensive reference guide providing per-MDP "look-fors", planning questions, aligned activities, and "talk moves", plus guidance on classroom organization, routines, policies, and climate. Quick tools include pocket-sized flip-books and activity cards designed as just-in-time supports that scaffold the consistent use of motivationally supportive strategies matched to NGSS science and engineering practices.
requirements: Teachers use the toolkit and quick tools during lesson planning and while teaching to incorporate the motivation principles into their teaching.
target_learning_goals: Integration of motivation design principles into daily science teaching routines
examples: Activity cards describe high-impact instructional strategies that incorporate multiple MDPs to support seamless integration.

title: Iterative co-design development cycle with design-implement-revise cycles
description: M-PLANS development used a co-design process bringing research and practice closer together, structured as a series of design-implement-revise cycles over three years. The team worked closely with science teachers to design concrete strategies usable in daily practice, studied program features as implemented in classrooms, and used what was learned to inform the next round, moving toward more refined and usable resources.
requirements: Requires collaboration with teachers and district-level science coordinators in successive cycles, with classroom study of each implementation round.
target_learning_goals: Development of professional learning resources that support student motivation in science
examples: The iterative process spanned 3 years, starting with initial design by the research team, followed by co-design cycles with participating teachers and district coordinators.
